title: Industropolis Run 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Industropolis Run Review: Batang Course, Weather, Cut-offs, Results
meta_description: Industropolis Run review from the 2025 race: a car-free AIMS course in Batang's industrial zone, 24°C and 89% humidity at 5am, cut-offs, 308 half finishers and winning times.
dek: What it was like to run the 2025 edition inside Batang's special economic zone: the car-free course, the humid dawn, the cut-offs and entry rules, how fast the field ran, and what changes for 2026.
verdict: Enter if you are an Indonesian citizen who wants a small, car-free, AIMS-certified half marathon or 10 km. The 2025 race, the first with a half marathon, drew 2,525 runners by the organiser's count; 308 finished the half, all inside the 210-minute limit, the last in 3:26:36. Tenth place in the half was 1:36:32 for men and 2:23:46 for women, so a good club runner can place. The catches: in 2025 the route climbed before the finish and runners bunched up near the jetty, which the reversed 2026 route is meant to fix, and dawn was humid, with 24°C and 89% humidity at 5am at the nearest airport. Book a room early: Batang's hotels were almost full.

sections.heading: The Course: Car-Free Roads Through an Industrial Zone
paragraphs: The race is run entirely inside the Kawasan Industri Terpadu Batang, the special economic zone at Gringsing on Central Java's north coast [1]. Before the 2025 race the organiser said the route would pass the industrial complex, rubber plantations, the reservoir lake and the Terminal Multipurpose Batang port, on roads closed to all vehicles that it described as gently graded [2]. After the race Yoyok Riyo Sudibyo, a member of parliament who runs, said there was nowhere else in Central Java or Indonesia to run a half marathon without a single car, and praised the mix of tarmac, countryside and sea [3].

The course is AIMS-certified [3]. It was not entirely flat. Announcing the 2026 race, the organiser said the new route would have no uphill stretch just before the finish, and that the course had been reversed after an evaluation of 2025 to stop runners bunching up [4]. The changes were made at crucial points including the jetty, and in 2026 runners go to the jetty first and then into the industrial area [4][5].

No route map, elevation profile or aid-station plan was published for 2025; the Race Guide link on the official site led nowhere [1]. School children cheered along the route [6], and the organiser had planned a jiring, a traditional cheering contest, among the surrounding villages [7].

sections.heading: The Weather: Humid at Dawn, 30°C by 8.30am
paragraphs: The nearest airport weather station is Semarang's Ahmad Yani airport, about 40 km east of the start. On race morning it recorded light rain at 3am, then 24°C at 5am, with a dew point of 22°C, 89% humidity and a 2-knot wind [8]. It warmed steadily: 25°C at 6am, 27°C at 7am, 28°C at 7.30am, 29°C at 8am and 30°C at 8.30am, by when humidity had fallen to 66% [8].

A dew point of 22°C means sweat evaporates slowly, so the early kilometres feel warmer than the thermometer suggests, and the back of the field finishes in the hottest part of the morning. The 2025 start times are not on any official page still online. For 2026 the registration page lists the half at 5am, the 10 km at 5.30am and the 5 km at 5.45am [9]; on that timetable a 2:30 half marathoner finishes at 7.30am, when Semarang was already at 28°C in 2025 [8].

sections.heading: Aid Stations, Cut-offs and Entry Rules
paragraphs: The rules promise a drinks station every 2 to 3 km along the course and at the finish [1]. The limits are 210 minutes for the half, 150 for the 10 km and 90 for the 5 km, with intermediate cut-offs to be announced before the race; runners outside the limit are recorded as DNF and get no medal [1]. The limits were not tight in 2025: the slowest of the 308 half-marathon finishers came in at 3:26:36 on the gun clock, and 43 took more than three hours [10]. Ten half marathoners did not finish and three were disqualified [10].

Entry is open to Indonesian citizens only, and the minimum age for the 10 km and half is 17, with a parent's letter required for younger runners [1]. Fees are not refunded, bibs cannot be transferred, and race packs are neither posted nor handed out on race day [1]. In 2025 the half cost Rp450,000, the 10 km Rp250,000 and the 5 km Rp200,000, before an early-bird discount [1][2]. Every entry included a race jersey, a timing-chip bib, a tote bag, a finisher medal, an e-certificate and insurance, and half-marathon finishers also got a finisher jersey [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The half marathon was close at the front and thinned quickly behind. The men's race was won in 1:17:59, with second and third in 1:18:06 and 1:18:39; fourth was more than five minutes back in 1:23:50, and tenth ran 1:36:32 [10]. The women's race was won in 1:36:37, from 1:40:26 and 1:48:58, and tenth place was 2:23:46 [10]. Only 39 of the 308 finishers were women, and the median finisher took 2:26:59 [10].

In the 10 km the men's winner ran 41:06 and tenth place 49:08; the women's winner ran 42:51 and tenth 1:05:46 [10]. The 2025 prize fund was Rp37 million, for men and women in the half and 10 km plus a best-costume prize [2]; the 5 km was a non-competitive fun run with no podium [1]. Open-category podium prizes go only to Indonesian citizens, decided on gun time [1]. A woman under 2:20 for the half or a man under 49 minutes for the 10 km would have made the top ten in 2025. For 2026 the organiser has invited national athletes and raised the prize fund to Rp100 million [4][5].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Accommodation is the pinch point. The regent said hotels in Batang were almost full over the 2025 race weekend [3], and hoped there would be a hotel inside the zone by 2026 [6]. Before the race the regency said it had lined up options from hotels to village homestays [7].

Packs must be collected before race day, in person or by someone carrying your letter of authorisation, proof of registration and copies of both ID cards [1]. For 2026, collection is at the industrial estate on Friday 4 December, 1pm to 6pm, and Saturday 5 December, 10am to 6pm [9]. The 2026 field is capped at 2,626 [4], with 350 places in the half, 1,300 in the 10 km and 976 in the 5 km [5].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you are an Indonesian citizen looking for a small, certified half marathon or 10 km on roads with no traffic at all, or a first half marathon with a generous limit: everyone who finished the half in 2025 did so in under 3 hours 27.

Think twice if you are not an Indonesian citizen, since entry is limited to WNI, or if you want a scenic city course: much of the route runs through an industrial estate. Plan for humid air at the start and book a room early.
The 2026 race is on Sunday 6 December, on a reversed route [4]. A route map, aid-station plan and intermediate cut-offs had not been published when this was written.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's rules and registration pages, the full results, airport weather records and Indonesian news reports.

faqs.question: Can foreigners enter Industropolis Run?
faqs.answer: No. The race rules open entry to Indonesian citizens (WNI) only, and open-category podium prizes also go only to Indonesian citizens. The minimum age for the 10 km and half marathon is 17, and younger runners need a letter from a parent. Entry fees are not refunded and bibs cannot be transferred to another runner.

faqs.question: Is the Industropolis Run course closed to traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes. The whole course runs inside the Batang industrial zone on roads closed to all vehicles, past factories, rubber plantations, a reservoir and the port, and it is AIMS-certified. In 2025 it climbed just before the finish and runners bunched up near the jetty; the organiser has reversed the route for 2026 to fix both.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at Industropolis Run?
faqs.answer: Not very fast by national standards. In 2025 the half marathon was won in 1:17:59 by a man and 1:36:37 by a woman, and tenth place was 1:36:32 and 2:23:46. The 10 km winners ran 41:06 and 42:51. For 2026 the organiser has invited national athletes and raised the prize fund to Rp100 million.

faqs.question: How hot and humid is Industropolis Run?
faqs.answer: Humid at the start and hot by the finish. On race morning in 2025, Semarang airport, about 40 km east, recorded 24°C with a dew point of 22°C and 89% humidity at 5am. By 8.30am it was 30°C with 66% humidity, so slower half marathoners finish in the hottest part of the morning.

faqs.question: Where should you stay for Industropolis Run?
faqs.answer: Book early. The regent said hotels in Batang were almost full over the 2025 race weekend, and the regency arranged options from hotels to village homestays. Race packs cannot be collected on race day; in 2026 collection is at the industrial estate on Friday 4 and Saturday 5 December, so plan to arrive by Saturday.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the review template, about the previous edition (7 December 2025). Weather is from Semarang airport METAR observations, about 40 km from the course, not a forecast. Full results were parsed from the SR.ID results table. The organiser's participant figure (2,525) differs from the entries listed in the results (2,690); the organiser figure is given as its own and finisher counts come from the results. The 2025 start times, route map and pack-collection details could not be found; 2026 start times are from the registration page (half at 5am), which conflicts with an aggregator's 4am. No readable runner accounts were found. No rating.
